page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-32 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 server family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon processor with 32 vCPUs, 16 physical cores, and 2 threads per core running at 2.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 24 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by top-tier capabilities in specific GPU-accelerated tasks alongside modest CPU performance. The server achieves top-tier results in large language model inference, processing 11863.44 tokens per second for small 135M model prompts and 2231.74 tokens per second for medium 7B model prompts. Conversely, CPU-bound single-core performance is weak, falling into the bottom 25% for stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the g2-standard-32 offers a specialized resource density that balances a mid-range CPU allocation with dedicated GPU acceleration. This makes it highly efficient for workloads that can offload computation to the NVIDIA L4 GPU, offsetting the weaker single-core CPU performance. It is optimally suited for AI inference, machine learning deployment of small to medium models, image processing, and ray tracing. It is less suitable for single-threaded CPU-bound applications or workloads requiring high-speed local storage.
